input_oneliner: 70F metastatic breast cancer admitted for dyspnea, tonight BP 84/56, HR 122, SpO2 91% 2L, RN reports she 'looks worse'

optional_context.comorbidity: metastatic breast cancer; admitted with dyspnea

reference_targets_freetext.item: Pulsus paradoxus measured by sphygmomanometer (>10-12 mmHg)
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: A large pulsus paradoxus is the single most useful bedside sign of tamponade in a patient with effusion

reference_targets_freetext.item: Jugular venous pressure (elevated in tamponade, RV failure/PE, and cardiogenic shock; low in sepsis or hypovolemia)
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Separates obstructive/cardiogenic shock from distributive or hypovolemic shock before fluids are given

reference_targets_freetext.item: Peripheral perfusion: capillary refill, cool or mottled extremities, and mental status
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Establishes shock physiology and urgency regardless of cause

reference_targets_freetext.item: Heart sounds (muffled), pericardial rub, and lung examination for crackles versus clear fields
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Muffled sounds with clear lungs favor tamponade; crackles favor left-sided cardiogenic shock

reference_targets_freetext.item: Ask about pleuritic chest pain and examine the legs for unilateral swelling
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Malignancy-associated pulmonary embolism is a close competitor

reference_targets_freetext.item: POCUS subxiphoid view for pericardial effusion with right ventricular diastolic collapse and IVC plethora
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Confirms effusion and tamponade physiology at the bedside

off_bedside_acceptable: CT pulmonary angiogram if PE suspected
should_not_recommend: Diuresis or positive-pressure ventilation before tamponade is excluded
Large fluid bolus without JVP and lung assessment
Deferring bedside pulsus paradoxus because an echocardiogram is ordered for the morning

perturbation_pair.changed_feature: metastatic breast cancer admitted for dyspnea -> anterior STEMI treated with PCI 2 days ago
perturbation_pair.input_oneliner: 70F anterior STEMI s/p PCI 2 days ago, tonight BP 84/56, HR 122, SpO2 91% 2L, RN reports she 'looks worse'
